How a content network reaches readers

Cloudflare operates a large public network that caches pages close to readers. Engineers pick it when they want fewer origin requests and a single place to terminate TLS. This article is about that product choice, not a challenge page.

A team still has to measure cache hit rate, decide which cookies vary the response, and watch origin error budgets. None of that is a gate in front of the document you are reading now.

The same tradeoff shows up with other networks. The useful question is which requests should stay dynamic and which can be cached for a day.
